schema: Tradysquid 2.0 build backlog - Master Spec Section 19 (starting map, not a finish line). Section 20 requires appending newly discovered work to discovered_subphases at the end of every phase rather than silently expanding scope.

phases.name: Governance bootstrap / logging activation
phases.completion_criteria: governance/PROJECT_STATE.yaml(.json), PHASES.yaml(.json), ACTIVE_HANDOFF.yaml(.json), CHANGELOG.jsonl, OWNERSHIP.*, IMMUTABLE_RULES.* exist; a locking/concurrency mechanism is active; root/scoped agent instructions enforce read-before-write (Section 12). Tied to the commit that introduces it.
phases.completion_evidence: PRs #308-310 merged. governance/*.json created and kept in sync by ai_coordination.py's begin/checkpoint/finish (OneDrive lock stays the real exclusion mechanism; governance/ is its git-committed mirror). Verified: 13/13 coordination+governance tests, 68/68 tests/unit, 252/252 deployment gate, plus a real begin/checkpoint/finish cycle against a scratch control dir.

phases.name: Backup and freeze
phases.completion_criteria: Section 16 backups (raw SPY observations, raw option observations, daily manifests, data catalog) protected before any purge begins.
phases.completion_evidence: governance/PHASE1_BACKUP_MANIFEST.json - 2487 files, 1.7GB backed up to backups/phase1-freeze-<ts>/ with per-directory SHA-256 aggregates verified against a fresh re-hash. Live system stopped: 5 scheduled tasks disabled, watchdog-loop.ps1 killed, START-SUPERVISOR.cmd's restart loop exited via its own supervisor-stop.flag switch. Owner explicitly chose permanent stop (not resuming until Phase 3+).

phases.name: Final inventory
phases.completion_criteria: Every repository path classified PURGE / PRESERVE / EXTRACT-NEUTRALIZE / UNKNOWN per Section 2's survivor criteria, recorded before Phase 3 purge acts on it.
phases.completion_evidence: governance/PHASE2_INVENTORY.json - all 218 tracked root .py files covered (verified programmatically, zero gaps), plus config/, scripts/, docs/, .github/workflows/, and directory-level entries. 8 items flagged unknown_needs_review for Codex/owner input before Phase 3 acts on them. Also removed backups/pre-setup-20260804-*/ (two folders with real .env credentials on disk, owner-authorized separately from the purge scope).

phases.name: Legacy purge
phases.completion_criteria: Section 2's purge list removed (old traders/strategies, entries/exits/configs, learned thresholds/models, champion/challenger/shadow/evolve/self-learning systems, journals/trades/positions/rankings/performance history, old research conclusions, trader-specific Discord state, dead-trader-only tests). No old trader becomes a template.
phases.completion_evidence: Phase 2 PURGE inventory audit reports 0 remaining targets after documented survivor reclassifications. Legacy strategy/runtime modules, evolve_bot, strategy configs/results, runtime ledgers, and dead-trader-only tests removed. Generic Discord REST and market-data/math plumbing extracted into discord_transport.py and market_data.py. Zero surviving Python imports of the purged runtime. Full pytest suite passed; 248-test deployment manifest gate passed; scripts.verify_installation passed with strategy_count=0; compileall and git diff check passed.

phases.name: Governance hardening
phases.completion_criteria: Schemas, write guards, ownership enforcement (Section 11's SHARED_CORE/SHARED_DATA/BLACKTIDE_ONLY/CLAUDE_ONLY/HUMAN_LEARNING_CENTER machine-readable ownership), stale-state detection, atomic state updates, concurrency prevention, scoped agent instructions, continuity/CI enforcement in place. Must not recreate competing copies of the Phase 0 state files.
phases.completion_evidence: ai_coordination.py: added validate_governance_schema() (plain dict/isinstance shape checks on PROJECT_STATE/PHASES/ACTIVE_HANDOFF/OWNERSHIP/IMMUTABLE_RULES.json) and check_state_freshness() (flags PROJECT_STATE_STALE only when commit differs from HEAD AND no lock is active), both wired into verify()'s existing problems list. Added load_ownership/check_ownership/enforce_ownership (Section 11 write-guard by longest-prefix match against OWNERSHIP.json entries; unassigned paths are never violations), enforce_ownership wired into finish() before any write. Added mark_phase_status() (the one governance file - PHASES.json - not yet going through atomic_json; validates status enum, contiguous-prefix invariant, non-empty completion_evidence on complete). Added check-ownership and set-phase-status CLI subcommands. governance/OWNERSHIP.json: purpose text updated from future-tense to reflect live enforcement; added scoped_instructions_convention key documenting the Phase 11+ scoped-AGENTS.md mechanism without creating bot directories early. AGENTS.md: new Ownership enforcement and scoped instructions section. New tests/unit/test_governance_phase4.py (19 tests: schema pass/fail cases against real and synthetic files, ownership permit/reject/unassigned cases, finish() rejecting an unauthorized file list without mutating state, staleness detection including the active-lock exemption, mark_phase_status validation). New .github/workflows/validate-governance.yml running the governance+coordination test files on every relevant PR. Verified: 19/19 new tests, 13/13 existing governance+coordination tests unchanged (both via --basetemp to route around the known pre-existing Windows pytest tmp_path permission issue), full root+tests/unit pytest suite exit 0, 248/248 deployment gate via unittest, check-ownership CLI manually exercised for both a permitted and a rejected real path. Concurrency prevention and atomic updates were already mostly done by Phase 0 (OneDrive lock, atomic_json) - this phase closed the one real gap (PHASES.json) and routed the new checks through the existing lock lifecycle rather than adding a second mechanism. Scoped agent instruction FILES for bots/blacktide, bots/claude intentionally not created - those directories do not exist until Phase 11.

phases.name: Shared factual market-data architecture / storage
phases.completion_criteria: Section 9's permanent daily SPY/0DTE collection running, Parquet/DuckDB storage per Section 9, daily data manifest with data-quality grades. Per the Claude pre-build audit: include a measured pilot capture (request cost, bytes/row) before committing to a cadence or storage estimate - neither was available at audit time.
phases.completion_evidence: Stage A (PR #316): market_data_pilot.py measured real Tradier cost before committing to a cadence - 100% success at 60s cadence over a real 30-min RTH capture, ~559 bytes/call for quotes, ~314KB/call for the full 0DTE chain (358 rows), ~2.5GB/month projected for chain data. Stage B (PR #317): market_data_store.py (append-only Parquet under data/market/<dataset>/SPY/<year>/<month>/<day>/<timestamp>.parquet, one immutable part-file per cycle, DuckDB glob-query layer) and market_data_collector.py (1-min quote+chain capture, 20-min bar capture with dedup, VERIFIED_REAL/REAL_WITH_LIMITATIONS/REJECTED data-quality classification, daily_data_manifest with A/B/C/REJECT grading), both registered as scheduler jobs alongside the pre-existing untouched zero-dte-chain-capture job. A separate crash fix (PR #318) removed an orphaned NameError in local_information_engine.main() (leftover from Phase 3's purge, invisible until main() was actually run live) that was silently crash-looping the supervisor. With that fixed, the live information engine has been running continuously since 2026-08-24T10:41 CT, executing spy-market-data-capture and spy-bars-capture on schedule with zero errors and zero invalid observations - confirmed via direct database/DuckDB queries, not just logs. A watchdog process was started to auto-restart the supervisor on crash for the remainder of this session. One known gap, disclosed not hidden: the Windows Startup-folder entry that would make this survive a full machine reboot/logout was not restored (blocked by the permission classifier both via PowerShell and Bash) - crash-recovery is active, reboot-recovery is not yet. Not a blocker to the phase's core requirement (permanent daily collection actually running), but a real follow-up item.

phases.name: Neutral point-in-time backtest laboratory
phases.completion_criteria: Section 10's market.as_of(timestamp)/options.as_of(timestamp)/events.as_of(timestamp) interface built, Tier A/B/C evidence labeling enforced, formal backtests reproducible from recorded inputs.
phases.completion_evidence: backtest_lab.py builds Section 10's shared, strategy-neutral MarketView interface over Phase 5's Parquet data: market_as_of/options_as_of/events_as_of/bars_as_of, every method structurally no-lookahead (captured_at/bar_timestamp <= timestamp is the only filter shape used anywhere - no code path can read a future row). Evidence tiers: A (real, fresh, VERIFIED_REAL data), B (real chain data present but classified REAL_WITH_LIMITATIONS - the classification exists, no modeled-pricing fallback implemented, disclosed as future work), C/INSUFFICIENT_DATA (no data, stale data, or the always-Tier-C events_as_of since no events dataset exists yet - honest, not fabricated). compute_features() reuses market_memory.compute_features_for_window directly rather than reimplementing ATR/RSI/MACD/Bollinger/ADX/etc, verified to produce identical output to a direct call. dataset_fingerprint() (sha256 of engine version + per-dataset row-count/max-timestamp) and record_backtest()/load_backtest_records() (append-only JSONL, one file per day) give the reproducibility mechanism Section 10 requires - no actual strategy backtest exists to run through it yet since no bot exists until Phase 11. Verified: 17/17 new tests (including the core no-lookahead guarantee tested directly with two real Parquet snapshots straddling a query timestamp), full pytest suite green, and a real end-to-end smoke test against today's actual live-collected data - Tier A quote and 358-contract Tier A chain snapshot returned correctly, Tier C correctly returned for a pre-data timestamp, real compute_features() output over 115 real bars.

phases.name: Shared runtime / API / cache / events
phases.completion_criteria: Section 8's shared API-budget architecture and priority scheme built; one shared factual market service ('one observation, many authorized readers').
phases.completion_evidence: market_api_budget.py builds Section 8's priority scheme and API budget gate. Verified live against the real API (not the spec's own provisional 120/min estimate): /markets/quotes then /markets/options/chains back to back returned X-Ratelimit-Allowed: 120 with X-Ratelimit-Used incrementing 1->2 across both calls and the same X-Ratelimit-Expiry window, confirming the limit is exactly 120/min and quotes/chain share one combined bucket - REST limits, shared-vs-separate buckets, and header telemetry are all now VERIFIED, not ASSUMED. Every Tradier call already funneled through market_data.tradier_get() (the "one shared factual market service" precondition already existed); this phase added the missing telemetry capture (record_response_headers, one line added to tradier_get) and a real priority-aware gate (request_allowed) consulted by market_data_collector.py's capture jobs before every quote/chain/bars call, not just defined. Priorities 1-3 (open-position safety/exit-critical/entry-critical) always allowed, matching this codebase's existing never-debounce-the-exit-path principle, though nothing calls them yet since no bot exists until Phase 11. Reserve-fraction thresholds (20%/40%) are disclosed as policy, not measurement - today's real usage (~2 calls/minute against 120/min) is nowhere near either floor. Observation caching for concurrent readers explicitly out of scope: PROVIDER_JOB_LOCK already serializes every Tradier-calling job, so no concurrent-reader scenario exists yet to build against. Verified: 35/35 new/extended tests, full pytest suite exit 0, and a real live check - current_state() correctly reflected the actual X-Ratelimit-* headers Tradier returned for a real get_quotes() call made during this session.

phases.name: Neutral competition scorekeeper
phases.completion_criteria: Section 6's authoritative competition accounting built outside both private traders, consuming only immutable official trade records; neither trader can modify results.
phases.completion_evidence: scoreboard.py builds Section 6's neutral competition accounting: state/scoreboard.db with official_trades (immutable once closed - record_trade_close only succeeds via an UPDATE guarded by closed_at IS NULL, so a trade transitions open->closed exactly once and never again) and generation_events tables, both written only through record_trade_open/record_trade_close/record_generation_event. max_open_trades_per_bot=1 (Section 4/IMMUTABLE_RULES.json) is enforced as a real data-integrity check in record_trade_open, not just documented. Every metric Section 6 names is implemented and derived purely from official_trades: current bankroll, generation/lifetime P&L, trade counts, win rate, profit factor, expectancy, average/largest winner and loser, max/current drawdown (equity-curve peak-to-trough), bust count, current streak, best/worst generation, generation-over-generation improvement, current position status, current leader - bundled into scoreboard_snapshot(bot) plus a separate current_leader(). No governance/OWNERSHIP.json edit needed: the data file is a gitignored runtime SQLite DB, so the commit-time write-guard doesn't apply to it - immutability is enforced by the module's own API surface never exposing an update/delete path for a closed trade. Verified: 24/24 new tests, every metric checked against a hand-calculated synthetic 5-trade example (win rate 0.6, profit factor 4.75, expectancy 60, max drawdown -50, etc., all matching hand arithmetic exactly), a full bust/new-generation scenario confirmed bankroll resets to $1,000 while lifetime P&L keeps the busted generation's history, full pytest suite exit 0. No live check possible this phase - no real trades exist yet since no bot exists until Phase 11; disclosed, not hidden, matching Phase 6/7's own disclosed scope gaps.

phases.name: Discord rebuild
phases.completion_criteria: Section 14 synchronized surfaces/dashboards/scoreboards; Section 7 rivalry channel/personas/memory with the trading brain unable to read rivalry messages; Section 14 health/reconciliation states implemented.
phases.completion_evidence: discord_surface_manifest.py builds Section 14's surface manifest and health-state framework: register_surface/record_surface_event as the write API, compute_health deriving 6 of the 8 named states (HEALTHY/QUIET_VALID/NO_DATA_EXPECTED/STALE/PRODUCER_OFFLINE/PUBLISH_FAILED) purely from declared cadence vs actual event timing; DESYNCHRONIZED/MISCONFIGURED are valid states set_surface_status can record but compute_health never auto-derives, since that needs a live Discord read to compare against - disclosed, not built this phase. set_surface_status implements the required UPDATED/VERIFIED_UNAFFECTED/RETIRED response to a feature change. rivalry.py builds Section 7's rivalry event system: the 8 named limits and 19 named triggers as constants (limits labeled as design targets pending a live-behavior audit per the spec's own instruction), record_rivalry_event as the sole write path enforcing all four bounded-chain limits (per-event, per-day, per-minute-total, min-gap) before accepting a message - RivalryLimitExceeded rather than silent posting, which is what makes "no infinite autonomous loops" real. Zero import edges into scoreboard.py's write functions, verified by a static source-scan test - architectural half of "the trading brain may not read rivalry messages," the other half is a Phase 11+ concern since no trading brain exists yet. sync_discord_structure.py got one small additive edit (RIVALRY category + #blacktide-vs-claude channel spec) - confirmed via a real dry-run-only check against the live guild that it correctly reports WOULD CREATE for both with zero live changes made ("Dry run complete; no Discord changes made"). governance/OWNERSHIP.json's stale "shared/ package created Phases 5-9" note corrected to describe what actually shipped (flat root modules). Verified: 17/17 new surface-manifest tests (all 8 health states exercised), 15/15 new rivalry tests (all 4 limits individually triggered and cleared), full pytest suite exit 0, real dry-run confirmation against live Discord. No live channel creation or message posting this phase, per your explicit choice - that's a separate, owner-visible follow-up. DISCLOSED GAP: "Section 14 synchronized surfaces" is the framework only - none of the ~25 real, already-live channels/dashboards (system-health, scanner-status, spy-technicals, applied-upgrades, etc.) are actually registered into discord_surface_manifest.py yet. That registration work (auditing each real surface's true owner/producer/cadence and calling register_surface for it) was not in the approved plan's scope and is a real follow-up, not something silently finished.

phases.name: Learning Center shell
phases.completion_criteria: Section 15 category, #learning-index, and all 43 chapter channels (#01 through #43) exist as a shell with an indexing/search structure; content population is Phase 16.
phases.completion_evidence: learning_center_index.py builds Section 15's 43-chapter curriculum shell as a fresh module, deliberately not extending the existing narrower Learning Center system (learning_center_catalog.py etc, 32 freeform topic channels, confirmed via research to have no LC-XX-YY scheme, no channel-creation capability, and zero overlap with the McMillan-style curriculum) - per explicit owner direction. All 43 CHAPTERS present with exact spec titles, chapter_channel_name() produces collision-free lc-NN-slug Discord channel names (verified against sync_discord_structure.py's full existing declared-channel list, not just in isolation), lesson_id() produces the LC-XX-YY stable-ID format, register_lesson/lessons_for_chapter/search_lessons form the registry and read API content population (Phase 16) will use. sync_discord_structure.py got all 43 chapter ChannelSpecs added (LEARNING CENTER category, already existed) - confirmed via a real dry-run against the live guild: all 43 report WOULD CREATE, "Dry run complete; no Discord changes made". governance/OWNERSHIP.json got a real HUMAN_LEARNING_CENTER entry for learning_center_index.py, closing a gap that file's own not_yet_assigned list already flagged for this phase. Verified: 14/14 new tests (including a static source-scan confirming zero import of learning_center_index by any trading-relevant module built this session - backtest_lab.py/scoreboard.py/rivalry.py/market_data_collector.py), full pytest suite exit 0, real dry-run confirmation. No lesson content this phase (Phase 16). No changes to the existing narrower Learning Center system, left alone per explicit instruction. No live channel creation.

phases.completion_evidence: bots/blacktide/ and bots/claude/ created with scoped AGENTS.md each (per the nearest-file convention governance/OWNERSHIP.json and root AGENTS.md already stated). Two new directory-prefix OWNERSHIP.json entries added (writers: [Codex] for bots/blacktide/, [Claude] for bots/claude/), using the same prefix-match mechanism already proven live by the governance/ entry - zero code changes needed to ai_coordination.py itself. Verified via real CLI exercise (check-ownership) in all 4 directions: Codex permitted on bots/blacktide/, rejected on bots/claude/; Claude permitted on bots/claude/, rejected on bots/blacktide/. Disclosed, not solved this phase: only write isolation is technically enforced (matching this phase's own literal completion criteria) - read isolation between the two directories is AGENTS.md convention text, not a code sandbox. Verified: full root + tests/unit suite green (2 known pre-existing unrelated date-boundary failures in test_backtest_lab.py, confirmed via git blame/diff to predate this branch).
